clue.text: Service perhaps not available after broadcast decried NHS

explanation.surface: A health service has been publicly criticised and now the service is unavailable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Service' looks like the NHS again, but here it is a set of crockery; the NHS is Britain's National Health Service.
explanation.definitionFit: Dresden china is fine porcelain from Saxony, and a dinner service of it is one example of a service.

clue.text: An EU administrative centre hanged a criminal

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged, taken as written

explanation.surface: Somewhere in the European Union, an administrative hub has executed a lawbreaker.
explanation.definitionFit: Den Haag, The Hague, is the Dutch seat of government and home to many international bodies, a European administrative city.

clue.text: Forms glossy surface on handle coated with odd bits of silver backing

going backwards, so the kept letters are read from the end in this down entry
the odd-numbered letters, first, third and fifth, are the bits kept

a handle is slang for a person's name

explanation.surface: Instructions for giving a silver-backed handle a glossy finish.
explanation.definitionFit: To enamel something is to coat it with a hard glossy layer, so enamels means forms such a surface on it.

clue.text: Master cutting extravagantly encased gold inlay on steel

indicators.note: one piece cuts into the other, sitting inside it

parts.note: MA, Master of Arts, is the degree abbreviation

explanation.definitionFit: Damascene is the craft of inlaying gold or silver patterns into steel, named after the metalwork of Damascus.

clue.text: Spies chest buried by Poles

explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' looks like Polish people, but it means the magnetic poles. Nark is British slang for a police informer.
explanation.definitionFit: A nark is a police informer, someone who spies on others and reports to the authorities.

clue.text: Retreat from all but frightful temperature

indicators.note: all but means everything except the final letter, which is dropped

parts.note: frightful in the sense of very ugly
T is the abbreviation for temperature

explanation.surface: Escaping from almost unbearable heat or cold.
explanation.definitionFit: A hideout is a hidden place to withdraw to, a retreat in the sense of a refuge.

clue.text: Poorer girl turned up in elevated check

explanation.definitionFit: Needier is the comparative of needy, so it means more in want, that is poorer.

clue.text: Stuns fat South African mountain idiot eating tons

berg is the Afrikaans word for mountain, as in the Drakensberg

T is the abbreviation for tons

explanation.surface: An overweight South African mountaineer gorges on tons of food and astonishes everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: To flabbergast someone is to astonish them completely, so flabbergasts is a synonym of stuns.

clue.text: See National Guard provide weapons to far-reaching power

parts.note: lo, as in lo and behold, means see
NG is the abbreviation for National Guard
to arm is to provide weapons

explanation.surface: Watch the National Guard being equipped with weapons to project power far afield.
explanation.definitionFit: The long arm of the law is an idiom for authority that can reach offenders wherever they go.

clue.text: Lamb, say, understood encounter as stated

parts.note: understood is read in the past tense, pronounced like the colour

explanation.definitionFit: Lamb is one example of red meat, along with beef and mutton, hence the 'say'.

the second set of letters to be rearranged

explanation.walkthrough: 'Book' looks like an instruction to reserve, but it is the definition, a noun.

clue.text: In darts, regularly inspired by drinks, we raise game

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter, taken at even intervals

parts.note: the second and fourth letters of darts

explanation.walkthrough: 'Raise game' looks like improving performance; in shooting, game is birds, and to raise them is to drive them up from cover.
explanation.definitionFit: Beaters are people employed on a shoot to flush birds from cover, so in the first person they say we raise game.

clue.text: Died in helping in Canadian sea hazard?

indicators.note: in places one piece within the other

parts.note: a slice is a helping of food
ob., from Latin obiit, is the abbreviation for died

explanation.surface: Someone died while helping out at sea off Canada.
explanation.definitionFit: Slob ice is a Canadian term for dense sludgy floating ice that hampers ships, a hazard at sea; the question mark admits the description is loose.

clue.text: Pollard closely packed trees to expose borders

parts.note: a hedge is a row of shrubs or trees grown close together

explanation.walkthrough: 'Pollard' reads as a gardening instruction, which is exactly what it does: it lops the top off.
explanation.definitionFit: Edges and borders are synonyms for the outer limits of an area, as nouns or as verbs.

clue.text: Son skipping exclusive exam concerning public choices

indicators.note: skipping means leaving out, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son
a select club is an exclusive one
an oral is a spoken exam

explanation.surface: A son misses an elite exam.
explanation.definitionFit: Electoral means relating to elections, which are the public's choices of representatives.

clue.text: Cut off in middle of Fleet Street having called journalist

indicators.note: the middle of a five-letter word is its third letter

parts.note: the central letter of Fleet
St is the abbreviation for Street
to call someone is to ring them, past tense rang
ed is short for editor, the crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A reporter in Fleet Street phoned and was cut off mid-call.
explanation.walkthrough: Fleet Street is the London street long home to Britain's newspapers, so the surface is about the press.
explanation.definitionFit: Estranged means no longer in contact or on good terms, that is cut off from someone.

clue.text: US commando having left instead of 2nd Engineers in recognition of fighting?

parts.note: the Green Berets are US Army special forces
L is the abbreviation for left
RE, the Royal Engineers, and it is the second occurrence of those letters that goes

clue.text: Excuse no one — bar should be raised

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one
bar and save both mean except, as in all bar one

explanation.definitionFit: An evasion is a dodge or pretext for avoiding something, so it can stand for an excuse.

clue.text: Foul goalkeeper? More or less

parts.note: a goalkeeper traditionally wears the number one shirt, No 1
some means approximately, as in some twenty people

explanation.surface: Was that a foul by the goalkeeper? Sort of.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foul' looks like a football offence, but it is an adjective meaning disgusting.
explanation.definitionFit: Noisome means offensive or disgusting, especially of smells, so it matches foul as an adjective.

clue.text: Second prominent feature of Stalin maybe in store

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second
a tash is a moustache, which Stalin famously wore

explanation.surface: Stalin's notable moustache is kept in reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: A stash is a hidden store or supply of something, so the two nouns are synonyms.

clue.text: The same hospital admits musician

clue.text: Plant workers going north stuck in possible suitable route?

parts.note: men as in workers on a site

explanation.walkthrough: The A1 is the long trunk road from London to Edinburgh; read as A-one it means excellent, hence suitable.
explanation.definitionFit: The anemone, or windflower, is a flowering plant of the buttercup family.

explanation.definitionFit: Stamina is the physical or mental strength to keep going, which is exactly a capacity for endurance.

clue.text: Saw advantage after removing lead weight, ultimately

indicators.note: removing takes those letters out of the word

parts.note: taken as written
the van, short for vanguard, is the lead of an army

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so only the last letter is used

parts.note: the last letter of weight

explanation.surface: Losing the lead weight gives the saw an advantage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like a tool or a verb, but it is a noun meaning a proverb.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is an old saying or proverb, so it is a synonym of adage.

clue.text: Put favourable slant on two levels about unknown philosopher

clue.text: Frolics in punts reported

explanation.definitionFit: Gambols are playful leaps and skips, so the noun is a synonym of frolics.
